# FsMcp 2.0

> Idiomatic F# toolkit around the official ModelContextProtocol .NET SDK for
> typed cancellable servers, Result-based clients, secure ASP.NET Core
> composition, testing, and enterprise-managed authorization.

FsMcp 2.0 is a breaking release. Primary tool, resource, prompt, typed, and
streaming handlers receive a final CancellationToken. Client resource reads
return the complete ResourceContents list. Server transport is selected by the
runner, not by the server computation expression.

## Author

- [Roman Melnikov (Neftedollar)](https://neftedollar.com/)

## Packages

- FsMcp.Core: domain types, validation, and serialization
- FsMcp.Server: server CE, cancellable handlers, stdio, and SDK DI composition
- FsMcp.Server.Http: Streamable HTTP and ASP.NET Core composition
- FsMcp.Client: typed client and enterprise-managed authorization
- FsMcp.TaskApi: pipe-friendly FsToolkit.ErrorHandling operations
- FsMcp.Testing: direct handler calls, assertions, and FsCheck generators
- FsMcp.Sampling: sampling types and explicit test helpers; legacy runtime wiring fails closed

## Runtime truth

- Use Server.run for stdio and FsMcp.Server.Http for Streamable HTTP.
- Use SDK request filters and ASP.NET Core middleware; legacy FsMcp middleware never ran and now fails closed.
- Stateful HTTP supports resource subscriptions with disconnect cleanup; stateless HTTP omits and rejects them.
- SamplingTool.define, DynamicServer, and legacy contextual notification wiring are obsolete/fail-closed.
- Enterprise-managed authorization is an HTTP client profile; the MCP resource server still needs authentication and authorization.
